4.text: In former times there were richer men among the Kavraˊlɪt than there

5.text: are at present. About forty years ago one of them bought horses and made

6.text: summer trips between the Reindeer camps, carrying his wares on horseback.

7.text: Another one, at his own request, was sent to Yakutsk by the officials of the

8.text: Kolyma district. He visited the Russian governor at Yakutsk, and received

9.text: through him a gold medal and a parade coat adorned with silver lace. At

10.text: present none of them equals in wealth Kuvaˊr and the other Eskimo traders

12.text: Several other regular trips, but of shorter range, are made for the pur-

13.text: pose of trading. In the Anui country Russian traders travel among the camps,

14.text: in winter with dog-teams and in summer with horses, collecting chiefly small

15.text: fawn-skins and white and red foxes. The Russian traders of the Anadyr do

16.text: not make such trips, and they do not go even as far as Holy Cross Bay;

17.text: indeed, neither the Russian traders nor the Cossack invaders cared to go

18.text: beyond the forest border, at least when travelling by land. On the other

19.text: hand, petty traders go in the winter-time with dog-sledges from every native

20.text: village of the Chukchee-Peninsula to the Reindeer camps, collecting large

21.text: fawn-skins and ready-made garments. Later in the summer whole squadrons

22.text: of boats start from Indian Point on their journey to Holy Cross and St. Law-

23.text: rence Bays, where the Reindeer people perform the ceremonial slaughtering

24.text: of the season. They return heavily laden with skins and meat. Some of the

25.text: boats go to the Anadyr and proceed upstream to take part in the large rein-

26.text: deer-hunts. Twenty years ago they proceeded along the seacoast to the Telqäˊp

27.text: summer camps, and as far as the Kerek villages. Here, near Capes Barykoff

28.text: and Navarin, was the southern limit of the Chukchee-Eskimo trade on the

30.text: UNITS AND PRICES. — The Chukchee trade is carried on exclusively in

31.text: barter. Money is quite unknown. The Reindeer people have not even a

32.text: word for it, and call it keliˊtul (“a piece of variegated”), which name may be

33.text: applied also to any piece of paper with writing on it. The Maritime Chuk-

34.text: chee call it manêˊman (from English “money” of the whalers).

35.text: The unit of value in Russian trade remains a bundle of tobacco “not

36.text: tampered with,” because the traders often abstract a few leaves and replace

37.text: the bindings. In recent years brick-tea has also come into use as a standard

38.text: of value, and is even preferred because of the uniform size of the bricks.

39.text: In the trade with whalers no particular unit is applied. Prices are very

40.text: variable, according to season and place. The same commodities are sold in

41.text: some places and seasons at prices two and three times as high as in others.
